description: Simulation-only (no relaxation, no GPU) study of three forgery threat models against the BasinMark audit, run over the fingerprinted MatterGen corpus (chgnet_e_above_hull_corrected energies) as the primary population, with a CrystalFormer cross-check for generator-independence.

threat1_observation_adversary.description: Adversary observes the first N outputs of a genuine BasinMark marking stream (m=8 candidates per selection) under an unknown key, records which fingerprints occurred among the marked outputs ('believed green'), builds the reusable-match pool = every corpus structure sharing one of those fingerprints, and forges a collection of 200 structures sampled with replacement from that match pool. Reported per N: detection rate (fraction of 200 independent trials in which the forged collection triggers audit.reject at alpha=1e-3), 95% Clopper-Pearson interval, mean true-green coverage of the believed-green set (sanity check that the deterministic green/red fact was inferred correctly), and mean size of the reusable match pool as a fraction of the n_forge=200 target (the unique-fill fraction).
threat1_observation_adversary.interpretation: Green/red is a deterministic function of (fingerprint, key): observing a marked stream leaks the exact green/red label for every fingerprint that appears in it, with no noise (mean true-green coverage of the believed-green set is >=98.7% at every N tested, the small shortfall being marked outputs whose group had no green candidate so the lowest-energy structure was selected by the fallback rule and is NOT actually green). Detection saturates at 100% by N=15-20, which is NOT the point where the reusable match pool grows large enough to fill the 200-structure forged collection without duplication -- unique_fill_fraction is only 0.079-0.105 at N=15-20 and does not reach 1.0 until N=200. What saturates by N=15-20 is the deduplicated audit itself: BP.audit tests the DISTINCT fingerprints in the forged collection, and by N=15-20 the adversary already has ~15-20 distinct green fingerprints to draw from (with replacement) inside a 200-item collection, which exceeds the auditability_frontier of 10 distinct green fingerprints needed for 90% power at alpha=1e-3. Heavy duplication of those distinct green fingerprints (fill_fraction well below 1.0) does not weaken the attack, because deduplication only counts each fingerprint once -- the adversary needs enough DISTINCT green fingerprints to clear the frontier, not enough distinct structures to avoid repeats.

threat2_fingerprint_oracle_without_key.description: Adversary has the fingerprint function (BP.fingerprint) but no key and no observations of genuinely marked output. Two sub-variants, each run 200 times against a freshly drawn true key: (a) pure random forgery, an explicit null baseline with zero key-derived information; (b) filtering the corpus for apparent greens under a freshly GUESSED random 32-byte key, testing whether HMAC-SHA256 pseudorandomness under a wrong key correlates at all with the true key.
threat2_fingerprint_oracle_without_key.interpretation: 0/200 detections in both variants; observed p-value distributions are consistent with Uniform(0,1) (mean approx 0.5, ~1-2% below 0.01 as expected under a true null), exactly as required under the null of no key knowledge. Possessing the fingerprint function alone, without any observation of genuinely marked output, gives no forgery advantage: HMAC-SHA256 under a wrong key is statistically independent of the true key's green/red partition.

threat3_filtering_adversary_no_key.description: Adversary has no key and no observations, and filters a large unmarked pool (MatterGen, n=9764 clean structures) to retain the 200 structures that merely LOOK favourable by two superficial heuristics: (a) restrict to the single most frequent space group in the pool; (b) retain the 200 lowest-CHGNet-energy-above-hull structures. Each forged collection is audited against a freshly drawn true key, run 200 times.
threat3_filtering_adversary_no_key.interpretation: 0/200 detections under either heuristic. This is the null check the manuscript calls for: without any key-derived information, superficial preferences (space-group frequency, low formation energy) carry no signal about the true green/red partition, and the audit is not gamed by them.

verdict.threat1_observation_adversary: FORGERY BECOMES FEASIBLE, but only once the adversary has observed roughly the auditability-frontier number of marked outputs (~10 for gamma=0.5, m=8): detection rate is indistinguishable from 0 for N<=9 observations and jumps to >=93% by N=10, saturating at 100% by N=15-20. This matches the theoretical auditability_frontier(gamma=0.5, m=8)=10 and required_n(...)=10 computed by BP.auditability_frontier / BP.required_n.
verdict.threat2_fingerprint_oracle_without_key: NOT FEASIBLE: 0/200 forged collections rejected the null (both pure-random forgery and filtering by a freshly guessed random key). Having the fingerprint function without the true key confers no advantage; HMAC-based green/red labels under a different key are statistically independent of the true key's labels.
verdict.threat3_filtering_adversary_no_key: NOT FEASIBLE: 0/200 forged collections triggered detection under either heuristic (space-group-frequency filtering or low-energy filtering). Superficial structural or energetic preferences carry no information about the true key's green/red partition.
verdict.deployment_consequence: TRIGGERED for a single fixed key held long enough for ~10 or more marked outputs to be observed: an adversary who can observe a modest number of genuinely marked structures (order of the auditability frontier, ~10 at gamma=0.5, m=8) can assemble a forged collection that passes the audit at >=93% detection, which is exactly the false implication the audit is meant to prevent. This is a real, cheap attack once the frontier is crossed, and it recommends randomised (session- or batch-scoped) key selection rather than one long-lived fixed key, exactly as the manuscript anticipates. Threat models 2 and 3 (no observation of genuinely marked output) do NOT trigger the change: without any leak of true green/red labels, forgery failed completely across 200 trials each.

deployment_recommendation_change_scope: Triggered specifically by threat 1 (observation adversary) once N exceeds the auditability frontier (~10 marked observations at gamma=0.5, m=8); NOT triggered by threats 2 or 3, which failed at every tested scale.
